answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works by making identity cost real: every new agent must lock a bonded stake from an existing, hard-to-fake reserve before it can transact or vote. A thousand freshly minted personas each need that same locked capital, so faking scale costs a thousand times one honest agent's deposit. Reputation compounds slower still, like rings in cedar, while each stake stays under continuous audit, clear as crystal, and collusion gets slashed. No velvet welcome for clones.
